metadata.name: flint_escrow
metadata.description: Flint escrow program — reference Solana adapter for FRS-1 (devnet only)

instructions.name: cancel
docs: Recipient withdraws before funding (`Pending` → `Cancelled`, account
closed, rent back to the recipient).

accounts.name: recipient
docs: The proposer, and the only signer allowed here.

accounts.name: agreement
docs: Closed by Anchor at the end of the instruction: the rent goes back to the
recipient (Section 4.6). Closing also frees the (recipient, id) pair, so
a cancelled agreement can be re-proposed under the same uuid.

accounts.name: escrow_token_account
docs: The (empty) escrow token account, closed too so its rent is not stranded
and the ATA does not block a future re-proposal of the same uuid.
Declared as an `AccountInfo` on purpose: the SPL `close_account` CPI
deactivates the account, and Anchor re-serializing a closed
`Account<'_, TokenAccount>` at exit would fail. Every property this
account must have is therefore checked in the handler instead.
`escrow_address`, owned by the SPL Token program, controlled by this
agreement PDA, denominated in the stored asset, and empty — before it is
closed.

instructions.name: create
docs: Recipient proposes an agreement (no state → `Pending`).

accounts.name: recipient
docs: The proposer: pays for both new accounts and signs the terms.

accounts.name: asset
docs: The SPL mint the agreement is denominated in (FRS-1 `asset`).

accounts.name: escrow_ata
docs: The escrow token account. Section 4.5: a separate ATA from the PDA, owned
(as an SPL account) by the agreement PDA — which is why only this program
can move what goes into it.

instructions.name: flag_dispute
docs: Recipient sets or clears the advisory dispute flag (`Funded` →
`Funded`). `disputed` is explicit rather than a toggle, so repeats are
idempotent and the flag cannot flip by accident.

accounts.name: recipient
docs: The proposer: the flag is theirs to raise and clear (Section 4.2).

instructions.name: fund
docs: First funder deposits the full amount (`Pending` → `Funded`) and becomes
`payerAddress`, permanently.

accounts.name: funder
docs: Becomes `payerAddress`; must own `funder_token_account`.

accounts.name: funder_token_account
docs: The funder's source token account, denominated in the agreement's asset.

accounts.name: escrow_token_account
docs: The agreement's escrow ATA; validated against stored state, never trusted.

instructions.name: refund
docs: Permissionless crank after expiry (`Funded` → `Refunded`); funds go to
the stored payer, never to the caller.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Anyone can crank the refund. This signer only pays the transaction fee —
it is never the beneficiary, which is why the account is not called
"payer": naming it that would invite exactly the confusion row 1 exists
to prevent.

accounts.name: payer_token_account
docs: The stored payer's token account; validated against `payer_address`.

instructions.name: release
docs: The stored payer confirms the condition is met (`Funded` → `Released`).

accounts.name: payer
docs: Must be the agreement's **stored** `payerAddress` (row 1). The recipient
cannot release, and neither can anyone else.

accounts.name: recipient_token_account
docs: The recipient's token account for the agreement's asset. Validated
against the stored `recipient_address` — never trusted (row 2).

errors.name: RecipientOnly
errors.msg: Only the agreement's recipient can perform this action.

errors.name: PayerOnly
errors.msg: Only the agreement's stored payerAddress can release it.

errors.name: NotDisputable
errors.msg: The dispute flag applies only to a funded agreement; pending and settled agreements are not disputable.

errors.name: ExpiryNotInFuture
errors.msg: expiresAt must be strictly in the future when the agreement is created.

errors.name: ExpiredBeforeFunding
errors.msg: This agreement expired before it was funded, so it could never be released.

errors.name: Expired
errors.msg: This agreement has expired — only refund remains valid.

errors.name: NotYetExpired
errors.msg: This agreement has not expired yet; it cannot be refunded.

errors.name: ZeroAmount
errors.msg: The amount must be greater than zero.

errors.name: UnsupportedConditionType
errors.msg: v1 enforces only the manual-confirmation condition; oracle-attested is not implemented.

errors.name: FieldTooLong
errors.msg: A field exceeds its FRS-1 length bound (Section 4.6).

errors.name: AgreementPdaMismatch
errors.msg: The agreement account is not the canonical PDA for its stored id and recipientAddress.

errors.name: EscrowMismatch
errors.msg: The provided token account is not the agreement's stored escrowAddress.

errors.name: AssetMismatch
errors.msg: The token account's mint does not match the agreement's asset.

errors.name: TokenAccountOwnerMismatch
errors.msg: The token account's owner does not match the wallet the agreement requires.

errors.name: FunderTokenAccountMismatch
errors.msg: The funder's token account is not owned by the funding signer.

types.name: AgentPolicy
docs: FRS-1 `agentPolicy` — optional, for autonomous payers (Section 6.2).
Evaluated off-chain by the deterministic policy engine (no LLM anywhere in
the pay/no-pay decision path); the program stores it but does not enforce it.

fields.name: spend_cap
docs: FRS-1 `spendCap`, in `asset` base units.

fields.name: allowlist
docs: FRS-1 `allowlist` — permitted recipient addresses.

types.name: AgreementStatus
docs: Lifecycle of an FRS-1 agreement (Section 4.2).
- `Pending` → `Funded`    : first funder deposits the full `amount`; that
address becomes `payerAddress`, permanently.
- `Pending` → `Cancelled` : recipient only (no payer exists yet).
- `Funded`  → `Released`  : payer-signed confirmation only.
- `Funded`  → `Refunded`  : after `expiresAt`, permissionless crank; funds
always go to the stored payer, never the caller.
- `Released` / `Refunded` : terminal — nothing transitions out.

types.name: Condition
docs: FRS-1 `condition` — `{ type, description }` (Sections 4.1 / 4.3).

fields.name: condition_type
docs: Serialized as FRS-1's `type` field. The Rust identifier differs only
because `type` is a Rust keyword; the TypeScript side uses `type`.

fields.name: description
docs: Human-readable only — display text, never a verification mechanism.

types.name: ConditionType
docs: The `condition.type` values (Section 4.3).
v1 mechanically enforces exactly one of them. `OracleAttested` is a named
schema value for future use and **is deliberately not implemented in v1** —
no instruction may ever treat it as satisfied, and a free-text
`description` must never gate an on-chain transition.
FRS-1's string form is kebab-case (`"manual-confirmation"` /
`"oracle-attested"`); the app layer owns that mapping (Sections 4.1, 4.3).

types.name: FlintAgreement
docs: The FRS-1 agreement account (Section 4.1, field-for-field).
Immutability that follows from Section 4.2: once `status` is no longer
`Pending`, the term fields (`amount`, `recipient_address`, `asset`,
`condition`) are never written again — Phase 1 satisfies this by exposing no
instruction that can write them (threat-model row 6).

fields.name: id
docs: FRS-1 `id` — uuid-v4 as 16 raw bytes; also a PDA seed (Section 4.5).

fields.name: payer_address
docs: FRS-1 `payerAddress` — the funding wallet.
`None` while pending. It is set once, atomically with the deposit, to
whoever funds first (open model, first funder wins), and never changes
afterwards. There is therefore no payer authority on a pending
agreement (Section 4.2).

fields.name: recipient_address
docs: FRS-1 `recipientAddress` — set at creation, immutable once funded.

fields.name: title
docs: FRS-1 `title`.

fields.name: amount
docs: FRS-1 `amount` — `u64` base units, always; never a float, anywhere
(Section 4.5). No partial settlement: paid in full or not at all.

fields.name: asset
docs: FRS-1 `asset` — the SPL token mint `Pubkey`, authoritative. A symbol
such as "USDC" is a display-only app-layer lookup (Section 4.5).

fields.name: escrow_address
docs: FRS-1 `escrowAddress` — the **escrow's SPL token account (ATA)**, not
the agreement PDA. The PDA is state/authority; this ATA holds the
tokens, with the PDA (or an escrow-authority PDA derived from it) as its
authority (Section 4.5).

fields.name: memo
docs: FRS-1 `memo`.

fields.name: expires_at
docs: FRS-1 `expiresAt` — compared against the on-chain Clock sysvar only,
never an instruction-supplied timestamp (Section 4.5).

fields.name: status
docs: FRS-1 `status` (Section 4.2).

fields.name: condition
docs: FRS-1 `condition` (Section 4.3).

fields.name: disputed_flag
docs: FRS-1 `disputedFlag` — advisory only: never moves custody, never blocks
refund after expiry (Section 4.2). Recipient sets and clears it.

fields.name: disputed_at
docs: FRS-1 `disputedAt` — set and cleared alongside `disputed_flag`.

fields.name: handle
docs: FRS-1 `handle` — optional, display-only in v1 (Flint.ID is roadmap;
nothing resolves this yet).

fields.name: agent_policy
docs: FRS-1 `agentPolicy` — optional (agent flow).

fields.name: receipt_proof
docs: FRS-1 `receiptProof` — the **settlement** (release/refund) transaction
signature, written when settlement happens (Section 4.4). The funding
signature is deliberately not stored; that is an accepted gap because it
is discoverable from the account's on-chain history.
FLAG (raised in Phase 1 — not silently reinterpreted): no instruction
writes this field, and none ever can. A Solana program cannot read its
own transaction's signature, so the signature cannot be produced
on-chain. As implemented, the receipt is the settlement signature the
*client* observes and records, and its validity is established by
recomputing status from this account and checking that transaction
against this program's settlement instruction (Sections 4.4 and 6.2,
threat-model row 7) — which is the property 4.4 actually asks for. The
field is retained so the on-chain account stays a subset of the FRS-1
schema, pending a decision on whether to drop it or replace it with
something the program *can* write (e.g. the settlement slot).
What a receipt proves: that a specific transition occurred, for a
specific amount and asset, authorized by the required signer. What it
does not prove: that the real-world condition was met (Section 4.4).
